status: Tracked release evidence. Engineering provenance, not legal advice. Records which source corresponds to the shipped binary, at which upstream commit, and with what digest. The archives it names were published at https://app.ourgalaxy.space/source/ on 2026-08-09 under GPL-3 6(d); this file is the tracked half and is not itself a publication record. It said NOTHING HERE IS PUBLISHED until 2026-08-09, which stopped being true the day the archives went live - the string is generated, so it had to change here or every regeneration would restore it.
what_this_is: One archive per component carrying a source-availability obligation, cut at the
exact upstream commit the shipped binary was built from, published
beside the binaries. This file is the tracked half: the commit, the digest, the
size, and the licence text captured at that same commit.
THE MODEL CHANGED ON 2026-08-09 AND THIS RECORD REFLECTS THE CORRECTED ONE.
The earlier plan was to hold the source privately and satisfy requests for it.
S&C read the clauses - docs/security/findings/SOURCE_OFFER_MODEL_CLAUSE_VERIFICATION_2026-08-09.md -
and found the written-offer routes in GPL-3 6(a) and 6(b) both begin "Convey the
object code in, or embodied in, a physical product". These binaries are
downloads. Those routes are unavailable, not merely unmet. 6(d) is what is left,
and it asks for "equivalent access to the Corresponding Source in the same way
through the same place" - which on-request delivery is not. This binds
ffmpeg.exe itself, LGPL-3.0-or-later through --enable-version3.
So these archives were published to /source/, next to the binaries, the way
the four archives already there were. Publication was an owner/OPERATIONS
action and happened on 2026-08-09; publication.state below records it.
The staged bytes live outside git. That is only acceptable because of this file:
every archive is refetchable from the upstream URL and commit SHA recorded here,
and the digest says whether what came back is the same source. Lose the staging
and it is rebuildable; lose this file and it is not.

publication.state: PUBLISHED 2026-08-09 at https://app.ourgalaxy.space/source/. Updated from STAGED, NOT PUBLISHED on the day the archives went live: this string is generated, so leaving it would have restored the stale claim on the next regeneration.
publication.destination: the same place the binaries are served from - the /source/ directory alongside ffmpeg-n8.1.1-13-g83e8541aa6-source.tar.gz, mpv-v0.36.0-403-g652a1dd907-source.tar.gz and ffmpeg-n6.0-source.tar.gz
publication.staging_path: Corresponding_Source/source/  (workspace root; flat, mirroring the destination so publishing is a copy)
publication.basis: GPL-3 6(d) / LGPL-2.1 6(d) / GPL-2 3 closing paragraph / MPL-2.0 3.2(a) - equivalent access from the same place. See docs/security/findings/SOURCE_OFFER_MODEL_CLAUSE_VERIFICATION_2026-08-09.md.
publication.who_publishes: owner / OPERATIONS. This script has no upload path and must not acquire one.
publication.why_not_in_git: Upstream source archives. Tracking them would weigh down every clone of the workspace repo for material that is byte-for-byte refetchable from the pins in this file.
publication.durability: NOT one of the disposable roots named in AGENTS.md (runtime/, docs/logs/, release-logs/, dist/, references/, Desktop_Builds/). Registered in docs/agent-control/workspace-layout-guide.md, declared Advisory in tools/quality/Assert-DurablePointers.ps1 so a durable record citing it says so out loud, and carries its own README.
publication.retention: GPL-3 6(d): "you remain obligated to ensure that it is available for as long as needed to satisfy these requirements." Retention is a licence condition once published, not a convenience.

pin_vs_release_note: A pinned commit that carries no upstream tag means no release tarball is this
source. fftw3 is the worked example: it is pinned five commits after the
fftw-3.3.11 tag while the binary self-reports fftw-3.3.11, so publishing the
3.3.11 release tarball would publish source that was not what was compiled.
The check is run for every component here rather than that one, and the
summary above says how often it comes back the same way.
version_claim_check is the sharper form of the same question. Where a version
was recovered from the shipped binary and corroborated against the builder pin,
that agreement is about the VERSION, not about the source: it does not mean the
pinned commit is the release. Each such claim is measured against its upstream
licence_texts_note: summary.licence_texts_missing is the number of components holding NO
licence text; the array above names them. Zero means every component in
scope carries at least one text captured at its own pinned commit, which
is the stronger evidence: a licence can change between revisions, so a
generic SPDX copy is not proof of what shipped with that source.
Zero here is a MEASUREMENT taken on this run, not a standing fact. It is
recomputed every time and will go non-zero the moment a component is
added whose pinned commit has no licence-bearing file at its root, which
is exactly when someone needs to be told.
Scope note: this counts the components in THIS record. It is not a claim
about transitive or vendored dependencies, whose licence texts are
tracked where those dependencies are enumerated, not here.
